claim: Whether a passing trim code exists for the sky130 trimmed D+ pull-up under local mismatch: for each Monte Carlo sample (one die) at least one of the 16 trim codes gives an effective resistance inside 1.425-1.575 kohm with the host 15 kohm load (trim selected at test), against spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 row 'FS device D+ pull-up' (1.5 kohm +/-5 % to 3.0-3.6 V), at tt (27 C, 3.3 V) and at the binding corner of the 45-point record sim/dplus-pullup-tolerance/records/20261020-174332-ca4a45a.md (ff, 100 C, 3.3 V). MOS mismatch comes from the `*_mm` library sections; the pinned PDK has no mismatch model for the ladder resistor (res_generic_po), so the ladder spread is an explicit testbench model with a named assumption, not a PDK claim. Schematic-level, no layout parasitics; not a signoff or catalog-tier claim.

corners.basis: binding corner of the 45-point record sim/dplus-pullup-tolerance/records/20261020-174332-ca4a45a.md: the largest best-code error (best_err_ohm 27.0493 ohm, best_r_ohm 1527.05) is at ff / 100 C / 3.30 V

control.description: 1 kohm in series with the D+ output (deterministic: adds to every code's effective resistance, so no code can reach 1.575 kohm or below) via the testbench rextra_ohm parameter

record.netlist_provenance: schematic-derived netlist: xschem export of design/dplus_pullup.sch (design/netlist/dplus_pullup.spice) with its five res_generic_po instances renamed to the testbench mismatch wrapper (sim/dplus-pullup-mismatch/testbench/dplus_pullup_mm.spice, generated by make_mm_netlist.py) plus the Monte Carlo testbench deck, frozen per campaign; no layout, no parasitic extraction
record.statistical_convention: Monte Carlo of local device mismatch only (monte_carlo.vary = mismatch): n = 400 samples per corner, base seed 166, per-sample seeds derived by `klt sim` (seed contract: sim.md 'Monte Carlo sampling'). Every g5v0d10v5 MOS instance draws independent mismatch (mc_mm_switch = 1 through the `*_mm` library sections). The pinned PDK has NO local-mismatch model for sky130_fd_pr__res_generic_po (empty statistics block; the global rp1 spread is off in the `*_mm` sections), so the ladder resistor spread is the testbench's own model: each of the five ladder resistors draws an independent relative error with sigma = A_R / sqrt(W*L), A_R = 1 %.um (W, L in um), an engineering assumption that is NOT derived from the PDK. Global process spread, including the resistor sheet resistance, is the separate corner axis and is not sampled
method: Stimulus: one pull-up instance per Monte Carlo sample (PU_EN = VPU = vsup), the trim code as the DC sweep variable (vcode 0 ... 15 at 1 step; TRIM<i> = bit i of the code, driven 0 / VPU by B sources; TRIM<i> = 1 shorts ladder segment i, code 0 = maximum resistance), the host 15 kohm from D+ to ground and a 1 mohm series resistor in the nominal campaign. All 16 codes therefore see the same mismatch draw, which is what trim-at-test selects from.

Measurement per sample: V(DP) per code; R_eff = (VPU - V(DP)) / (V(DP)/15000) per code, as in sim/dplus-pullup-tolerance; `err_cNN_ohm` = |R_eff - 1500|; `best_err_ohm` = the minimum over the 16 codes; `n_in_window` = the number of codes with |R_eff - 1500| <= 75 ohm (inclusive 1.425-1.575 kohm).

Graded per sample (each its own yield measurement, target_yield 0.99 at 95 % confidence): `best_err_ohm` <= 75 ohm and `n_in_window` >= 1, which are the same event stated twice (a sample passes when some code is inside the window); a sample with no passing code counts as a failing sample. A recorded run in which the yield claim is not supported (including a 'no passing code' outcome) is a FAIL record: the failure is the result, not a waived row.
Selection limit: the code is chosen per sample (per die, as at test) and per corner; the record does not show that one calibration code survives voltage and temperature after trim at one condition.

Each corner is its own population (one `klt sim` Monte Carlo request, backend batch, per corner); nothing is pooled across corners. `klt yield-samples` pairs each nominal campaign with its negative-control campaign (same deck, same seeds, 1 kohm in series), and `klt yield` grades the pair.

Negative control (deterministic): 1 kohm in series with the output adds 1 kohm to every code, so no code can be inside the window and `n_in_window` is 0 on every sample; the yield report must flag both graded measurements `detected`.

Mismatch activity: a non-zero sample stddev of `best_err_ohm` (yield report `distribution`) is the evidence that the draws reached the circuit; the ladder spread is the testbench model named above, the MOS spread is the PDK's.
PDK: the pinned open_pdks revision of sim/pdk-pins.json (current pin); each record states the revision and the model library sha256.
record.footer: Scope: schematic-level statistical evidence for one block against the ratified D+ pull-up resistance row, at the corners named in the record. Local mismatch only: MOS mismatch from the PDK and an explicit, assumed ladder-resistor spread (A_R = 1 %.um); global process spread, including the resistor sheet resistance, is covered by the deterministic corner records; the corner x mismatch combination is limited to the corners named. It does not show that one trim code survives voltage and temperature, and does not claim the pull-up supply, trim storage, layout, DRC/LVS or signoff, and does not relax any target. A FAIL record is evidence of failure, not compliance.

yield.sample_size_justification: target_yield 0.99 at 95 % two-sided confidence: with zero observed failures the exact (Clopper-Pearson) lower bound reaches 0.99 only for n >= 368 (klt yield `required_n_for_target`), so n = 400 per corner is the smallest round count that can support the claim; the +/-0.01 precision target needs n >= 183. A failing row is not rescued by a larger n: it is recorded as failing.
